# HealthPath (IATRIC) — project notes for AI sessions

Read this **only when the task touches these areas**. It is deliberately a normal doc
(not a `.clinerules` file) so it costs zero context until it is opened.

## Stack / commands
- Next.js 14.1 pages router (`pages/`), plain JS/JSX (no TypeScript) under `src/`.
- React 18, react-bootstrap 1.6.1, redux 2.5 (`@reduxjs/toolkit`), swiper 7, MUI (Dialogs/NoSsr), firebase + firebase-admin.
- Constants + API map: `src/constant.js` (`api.*`) | i18n: `src/i18n/translations.js` (`useLanguage().t(key, fallback)`) | store: `src/store/store.js` + `src/store/slices/**`.
- Styles: per-feature CSS modules + `styles/globals.css` + `public/css/customStyle.css` (site CSS overrides bootstrap form controls: `.appointment-form .form-control` height, `.form-group` padding). `.consultation-btn` lives there too — it is the shared CTA (`ConsultationButton`): its font-size uses `clamp(16px, 1.6vw + 9px, 24px)` and on ≤575.98px it wraps instead of overflowing, because heroes wrap it in narrow (50%) columns. Keep that responsiveness when touching it.
- `ConsultationButton` (`src/components/Common/commonUi.js`) accepts an opt-in attention variant: `variant="book-now"` (or the `isBlinking` alias) appends `.consultation-btn--book-now`, a subtle green glow pulse (`@keyframes consultationBtnPulse`, 2.4s, box-shadow ring + tiny opacity dip) defined in `public/css/customStyle.css` and **disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`**. Applied only to the five "Book Now" CTAs (`Header1` ×2, `Tabs-1`, `Appointment/CommonHealthConcern`, `Demo5About2`) — every other instance keeps the plain `.consultation-btn` class. Note the component ignores a passed `className` (pre-existing behaviour, deliberate).
- Verify with `npx next lint`; full build with `npm run build`; e2e specs live in `tests/` (excluded in `tsconfig.json`) and run with `npm run test:e2e`.
- DB from `.env` (`MONGO_URI`): **`IATRIC_test`**. Read-only checks are easy with `node -e` + mongoose run from the repo root.

## Super-admin & API conventions
- Panels use react-bootstrap (Modal/Form/Row/Col); tag/chip UI uses inline styles; local component state, no new store slices.
- Service options: redux `superAdminHomePage.serviceOffered` (fetched from `api.serviceOffered`), filter `option.isActive !== false`.
- Consultation types: `superAdminConsultationtype` (Audio, Video, Home visit, Clinic).
- Doctor model `src/models/doctorModel.js`: `consultationType` and `serviceOffered` are arrays (`serviceOffered` required); there is **no `speciality` field**.
- Super-admin **Add Doctor** (`src/components/superAdminComponent/AddDoctor/AddDoctorForm.js`) mandatory fields: name, email, mobile number, area of expertise, degree, language, work experience, consultation type, services offered, work days, overview. Everything else (gender, education + training, passwords, price, doctor share, picture/certificates/stamp/signature, slot times) is optional — the matching `required` flags in `doctorModel.js` were relaxed so such a POST succeeds, and `gender` lost its accidental `unique` index (a unique gender index makes a second doctor of the same gender impossible). `consultationType`/`serviceOffered` are validated in `handleSubmit` because their <select> always keeps `value=""` (HTML `required` cannot fire); both are submitted comma-joined and `pages/api/addDoctor.js` splits them back into arrays.
- FormData PUTs must append every editable array field or `pages/api/addDoctor.js` drops it; that PUT parses comma-joined strings into trimmed arrays (`consultationType`, and `serviceOffered` only when the client sends it).
- Work days use the shared chips `src/components/Common/WorkDaysPicker.js` (Mon–Sun toggles, inline styles, aria-pressed with the full day as the accessible name) in **both** the Add Doctor form and `DoctorModalComp`. Helpers live in `src/customUtils/workDays.js`: state is an array of canonical day names, but `workDays` is submitted/stored as a **comma-joined String** (`formatWorkDays`) because `doctorModel.workDays` is a String and `pages/api/addDoctor.js` forwards it verbatim — never send an array: **mongoose 8 silently drops an array assigned to a String path** (the field disappears from `$set`, so the approval PUT `Doctor.findByIdAndUpdate(id, changedFields)` would blank it). `parseWorkDays` reads legacy free text ("mon-sunday", "Mon - Fri", "Monday & Wednesday") so edit mode pre-selects correctly, and `formatWorkDaysLabel` renders the compact "Mon – Fri" in the doctor list (falls back to the raw value when nothing parses). Both forms block submission with an inline "Please select at least one workday"; in `DoctorModalComp` the picker only rewrites `editedDoctor.workDays` when a chip is clicked, so the doctor-panel approval diff keeps reporting "no change" for untouched legacy values.
- Education + training is a **repeatable** field: `doctorModel.educationTraining` is `[String]` (it used to be a String) so one doctor can list several degrees. Helpers live in `src/customUtils/educationTraining.js` and are the single source of truth: `parseEducationTraining(value)` normalises anything (array → trimmed/de-blanked entries; legacy string → split on **newlines/semicolons only, never commas** because a degree may contain one; `null`/`""`/`[]` → `[]`), `formatEducationTrainingLabel` renders the " · " joined label used by the public `Doctor1Details` page, `appendEducationTraining(formData, value)` writes the FormData. The UI is `src/components/Common/EducationTrainingInput.js` (one row per entry, the remove button is disabled while a single row remains, "+ Add Education / Training"), wired into **both** the Add Doctor form (rows in their own `educationItems` state) and `DoctorModalComp` (draft rows from `parseEducationTraining(doctor.educationTraining)`, `editedDoctor` only rewritten when a row is edited so an untouched legacy value still reports "no change" in the doctor-panel diff). Blank rows are dropped on submit. Each entry travels as its **own repeated FormData field** (`formData.append("educationTraining", item)`), because the `fields → stringFields` spread in `pages/api/addDoctor.js` comma-joins repeated fields; the API therefore parses `fields.educationTraining` directly (the raw array) and overrides the spread — on POST always, on PUT only when the field is present, where a present-but-blank field means "clear the list" (that is how the form signals "every entry deleted"; `appendEducationTraining` always appends at least one field). Mongoose casts a leftover legacy String to a one-element array and does **not** split it on commas, so stale clients cannot corrupt a degree.
- Doctor profile edits are APPROVAL-BASED: `RegisterDocLoginHeader.handleSaveDoctor` diffs fields (arrays element-wise) and POSTs `{changedFields}` to `/api/registerDoc/doctorUpdateReq` → stored in `src/models/docDetailsChangeReqSchema.js` → applied only when a super-admin PUTs `?action=approve`. New doctor fields must be primitive/array-comparable so the diff detects them. **Any value in `changedFields` must be a string/number/array** — a `File` serialises to `{}`, so the Doctor Panel uploads the photo first and sends only its URL (see the profile-photo note below).
- The doctor profile modal is the shared `src/components/superAdminComponent/DoctorModalComp.js` (used by the super-admin doctor list **and** the doctor's own header) — keep both panels working.

## Doctor panel (registerDoc)
- Routes `pages/registerDoc/{login,homepage,viewAllAppointment,prescription,doctorEarnings}.js`; each wraps content in `<DoctorAuthenticatedComponent>` + `<Layouts header={9} footer={7}>`.
- Data: `state.appointment.{appointments,todaysAppointments,doctorEarnings}` from `src/store/slices/registerDoc/appointmentSlice.js`.
- Endpoints via `api.*` (`updateDoctorStatus`, `doctorUpdateRequest`, `leaveRequest`, `doctorEarning`, `prescriptionCall`); handlers in `pages/api/registerDoc/`.
- Styles: per-feature CSS modules (`HomePage/StatsCard/DoctorEarnings/DoctorLogin/ManageSlotsModal/GeneratePdf .module.css`); dialogs in `registerDocComponent/model/`; helpers in `registerDocComponent/utils/{constant,helper,helperApi}.js` (helperApi uses axios).
- Prescription/print: `prescriptionComp.js` + `lib/{DoctorPrescriptionGenerator,MedicineForm,FrequencyTimeSelector,DoctorStampGenerator}.js`; section labels are local constants in `utils/constant.js` (not i18n).

## Website services/speciality (single source of truth)
- `state.globalData.{services,speciality}` (`src/store/slices/bookingWebsite/globalDataSlice.js`): `setServiceOfferedData(payload)` filters `isActive !== false` and splits by `categoryType` — MAJOR → `services`, SUB → `speciality` (missing value counts as MAJOR).
- Read it through `useGlobalData()` (`src/customUtils/useGlobalData.js`); never import `speciality` from `src/constant.js`, never read `state.superAdminHomePage.serviceOffered` on the website (that slice is super-admin only).
- Blended fallback: slice when populated, else the static lists (`src/constant.js` `speciality`, `data/services.js` `servicesData` / `AllDepartmentService` / `demo5ServiceHighlights`).
- Presentation assets (icon/image/slug/description) stay keyed by NAME via `getServiceAsset()` / `mergeServiceLists()`; DB membership + order win, unknown names render with defaults.
- Writers: `UtilService.fetchBasicConfiguration` (homepage) and `BookConsultationApiCall.getServiceOffered` (appointment page) dispatch `setServiceOfferedData`; the hook fetches once when the slice is empty.
- DB collection for serviceOffered rows: **`servicesoffereds`** (mongoose pluralises the `servicesoffered` model): 9 MAJOR, 11 SUB.
- A doctor's specialities live in `doctor.serviceOffered`; the appointment form matches with `matchesSpeciality()` in `src/components/Appointment/Appointmentform.js` (case/slug/partial), never `doctor.speciality ===`.
- DB-driven lists need an icon fallback keyed by name (`ICON_BY_NAME` + default icon in `Demo5Services1` / `Demo5Services2`).

## Marketing panel (Phase 1)
- Client: `src/marketing/components/**` (`MarketingAuthGuard`, `MarketingLogin`, `MarketingDashboard`, `blocks/*`, `css/marketingPanel.module.css`).
- Routes: `pages/marketing/login.js` (`/marketing/login`) and `pages/marketing/index.js` (`/marketing`, guarded). Standalone pages — they do NOT use `src/layout/Layouts.js`.
- API routes (root `pages/api`, not `src/pages/api`): `pages/api/marketing/{auth/login,auth/logout,auth/session,modules}.js`.
  Server helpers/utils live in `src/api/marketing/{helpers,utils}` — never under `pages/`, or Next exposes every module as a public endpoint.
- Session: HMAC-signed token in an httpOnly `marketing_session` cookie (Node `crypto`, no deps, 8 h TTL). Helpers: `src/api/marketing/utils/token.js`, `src/api/marketing/utils/validation.js`, `src/api/marketing/helpers/apiHandler.js`, `src/api/marketing/helpers/requireMarketingAuth.js`.
- Cookie flags: `Secure` is added only for real HTTPS requests (`x-forwarded-proto: https` / TLS socket) or when `MARKETING_COOKIE_SECURE=true`. Do NOT tie it to `NODE_ENV` — a production build served over plain HTTP (e.g. `http://192.168.x.x:3000`) would silently drop the session and bounce the user back to the login page.
- Login trims username/password (mobile autofill and paste often append a space) and lowercases the username; failures answer with a `reason` (`missing` / `username` / `password`) so the form can name the wrong field. The form also verifies `/api/marketing/auth/session` right after a successful POST and reports an explicit "browser did not keep the session cookie" message instead of silently redirecting back.
- Credentials (Phase 1, server-side only): `marketing@healthpath.com` / `Marketing123!` — override with `MARKETING_USERNAME` / `MARKETING_PASSWORD` / `MARKETING_SESSION_SECRET`.
- `api.*` in `src/constant.js`: `marketingLogin`, `marketingLogout`, `marketingSession`, `marketingModules`; sessionStorage key `marketing_info_local_storage`.
- Next phases: 2 SEO keywords (model + CRUD + `next/head`), 3 popup banner (DB + Firebase upload/schedule; `BannerPopup` then reads the API), 4 Demo5Blog1 content, 5 DB-backed marketing user + hashed password + rate limiting.

## Marketing panel — SEO keywords module (Phase 2)
- Model `src/models/marketingPanelSchema.js` — model `MarketingPanel`, schema option `{ collection: "marketingPanel", minimize: false }` (the explicit name is required; mongoose would pluralise to `marketingpanels`, and `minimize: false` keeps the reserved empty objects). One document per site page: `pageIdentifier` (unique, lowercase), `pageTitle` (drives the `<title>`), `seoKeywords[]`, `metaDescription`, `isActive`, `updatedBy`, timestamps, plus `bannerPopup: {}` / `blogDetails: {}` reserved for Phases 3–4.
- API (session required): `pages/api/marketing/seo/index.js` — GET list, POST create/upsert-by-`pageIdentifier`, PUT partial update by `_id` (publish toggle + field edits, with a duplicate-identifier guard), DELETE `?id=`. Public read-only: `pages/api/marketing/seo/metadata.js` (`?path=/`, 60 s cache, active rows only). Queries live in `src/api/marketing/helpers/seoQueries.js`.
- `pageIdentifier` ↔ route map: `MARKETING_PAGES` in `src/api/marketing/utils/seoPayload.js` (`home` → `/`, `services` → `/all-services`, …) with `pathToPageIdentifier()` / `identifierToPath()`; add new pages there.
- Shared payload rules live in `src/api/marketing/utils/seoPayload.js` (`normalizePagePath`, `sanitizeSeoPayload`, `SEO_LIMITS`) and are imported by both the API and the form — keep it free of server-only imports.
- UI: dashboard tile `src/marketing/components/SEOKeywordsCard.jsx` (pure navigation - no form controls in it) → route `pages/marketing/seo.js` → view `src/marketing/seo/index.jsx` → dialog `src/marketing/components/seo/EditSEOModal.jsx`. Shared chrome for every marketing screen: `src/marketing/components/MarketingShell.js`.
- react-bootstrap here is **1.6.8**: use `<Form.Control as="select">` (there is no `Form.Select`), and no `Form.Floating`.
- Site wiring (server-side, Option A): the 15 pages in `MARKETING_PAGES` export `getStaticProps = () => getSeoStaticProps("/path")` (`src/api/marketing/helpers/seoServer.js`) → they build as `● (ISR: 60s)` while all other pages stay `○` static. `pages/_app.js` passes `pageProps.seoMetadata` into `<SeoMetadata metadata=…>`, which renders `<title>`, `meta description`, `meta keywords`, `og:title/description/type` (canonical + `og:url` only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is set). Panel POST/PUT/DELETE call `res.revalidate(identifierToPath(...))` so a save rebuilds that page immediately (no-op in dev).
- `<SeoMetadata>` must stay OUTSIDE `<NoSsr>` and `<PersistGate>` in `pages/_app.js`: both render nothing on the server, so anything inside them can never appear in the HTML that crawlers receive. Pages without server props fall back to a client fetch.
- `src/lib/db.js` keeps its connect promise **module-scoped** (never on `global`): the page bundle and the API bundle can hold different mongoose copies while `global` is shared, which made one bundle believe it was connected ("buffering timed out"). Do not reintroduce `global.mongoose`.
- Env/DB split: `.env` (dev, `next dev`) → **`IATRIC_test`**; `.env.production` → **`IATRIC`**. `npm start` runs a custom `NODE_ENV=production node server.js` (and `next start` also loads `.env.production`), so a built app writes to `IATRIC` — check the right database before/after tests.
- `api.*` additions: `marketingSeo`, `marketingSeoMetadata`.
- Next: Phase 4 Demo5Blog1 content, Phase 5 hashed DB user.

## Auth, sessions & logout redirects (domain-independent)
- Login/logout go through next-auth (`pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js`, credentials providers `superAdmin-credentials` / `doctor-credentials`); both panels call `signIn(..., { redirect: false })` (`src/helper.js`) and navigate with `router.push` themselves.
- **Fixed bug (production SuperAdmin logout landed on `http://localhost:3000`)**: next-auth 4.24 resolves the server origin in `utils/detect-origin.js`, which returns `process.env.NEXTAUTH_URL` **verbatim** (otherwise the library default `http://localhost:3000` from `utils/parse-url.js`), and `defaultCallbacks.redirect()` returns `` `${baseUrl}${url}` `` — an **absolute** URL. `.env.production` shipped `NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000`, so `signOut({ callbackUrl: "/superAdmin/onload", redirect: true })` navigated the browser to `http://localhost:3000/superAdmin/onload`. The **client** next-auth was never the problem (`client/_utils.js#apiBaseUrl` returns the relative `/api/auth` basePath in the browser) — only server-built redirects carried the bad host. The same stale value also set `useSecureCookies = false`, i.e. no `__Secure-`-prefixed session cookie in production.
- Fix is on both layers: (1) `.env.production` → `NEXTAUTH_URL=https://healthpath.co.in` (must be the real https origin; `.env` keeps localhost for `next dev`); (2) `pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js` builds its options **per request** and overrides `callbacks.redirect`: same-site targets are re-anchored to the origin of the live request (`getSameSiteOrigin`), absolute URLs are honoured only when they point at this deployment, fallback `<origin>/`. Helpers in `src/lib/appOrigin.js` (`getRequestOrigin` reads `x-forwarded-host`/`x-forwarded-proto` then `Host`, plus `getConfiguredAppUrl`, `getSameSiteOrigin`, `toRelativePath`, `isTrustedRedirectUrl`).
- ⚠️ **The redirect callback must return an ABSOLUTE URL.** next-auth's own client (`next-auth/react/index.js`) parses it with `new URL(data.url).searchParams` for credentials sign-in when `redirect: false`, so returning a bare relative path crashes the login with `Failed to construct 'URL': Invalid URL` (it happened once: the callback briefly returned `/superAdmin/onload`). `baseUrl` handed to the callback is the detected *origin* only (`core/lib/callback-url.js`), used here as the last-resort origin.
- Client logout call sites — `src/components/superAdminComponent/NavBarComponent/RightSideMenu.js`, `src/components/registerDocComponent/NavBarComponent/RightSideMenu.js`, `src/layout/Header/RegisterDocLoginHeader.js` — call `signOut({ redirect: false })`, clear their `sessionStorage` key, then `window.location.replace("/<relative path>")`. Keep that shape: `redirect: true` hands control back to the server-built (origin-dependent) URL.
- Other `localhost` fallbacks removed: `src/lib/socket.js` falls back to `window.location.origin` (socket.io uses `window.location` when no URL is passed) and `src/lib/cashfree.js` builds its return/notify host from `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEVELOPMENT_PRODUCTION_URL` → configured app URL → localhost **only outside production** (throws instead of sending a paying patient to localhost). Nothing in `src/` hardcodes a redirect host any more.
- Verify without a DB: `next dev`, then `GET /api/auth/csrf` (keep the cookie) and `POST /api/auth/signout` with `csrfToken`, `callbackUrl=/superAdmin/onload`, `json=true` → `{"url":"http://localhost:<port>/superAdmin/onload"}` (absolute and `new URL()`-parseable). With `x-forwarded-host: healthpath.co.in` and `NEXTAUTH_URL=https://healthpath.co.in` it returns `https://healthpath.co.in/superAdmin/onload`; a foreign `callbackUrl` (or a stale `http://localhost:3000/...` cookie value) collapses to `https://healthpath.co.in/`. Run every returned value through `new URL()` - a relative one reproduces the client-side login crash.

## Marketing panel — homepage banner (Phase 3)
- **Inline on the dashboard** (no separate page): `src/marketing/components/banner/HomepageBannerCard.jsx` renders the block (thumbnail, Active/Paused badge, "Last updated", storage path) and hosts `src/marketing/components/banner/EditBannerModal.jsx` (drag & drop + file picker + live preview + "Save & Replace").
- Storage: the `bannerPopup` field of the **`home`** document in `marketingPanel` — `{ bannerUrl, altText, href, isActive, lastUpdated, updatedBy }`; helpers in `src/api/marketing/helpers/bannerQueries.js` (upsert creates the home doc when the panel is empty).
- Firebase: `src/services/firebaseStorage.js` uploads with **overwrite** to the fixed path `metadata/img.png` (`uploadBannerImage`). Uploads are first downscaled + re-encoded to WebP **in the browser** (`optimizeImageFile`: max 1600px, quality 0.85, returns the original file when canvas/codecs are unavailable) and stored with `cacheControl: public, max-age=31536000`; `applyBannerCacheMetadata()` (called best-effort from `HomepageBannerCard`) repairs objects uploaded before that change. `withCacheBuster(url, lastUpdated)` versions every rendered URL so a replaced image is never served from cache. (The old `sendBannerToFirebase()`/`images/popupBanner/` upload path no longer exists.)
- API: `pages/api/marketing/banner/index.js` (guarded GET/PUT, stamps `lastUpdated`) and `pages/api/marketing/banner/metadata.js` (public, 30 s cache, returns nothing unless active AND a URL is stored).
- UI: dashboard tile `src/marketing/components/PopupBannerCard.jsx` (navigation only, shows the current status) → `pages/marketing/banner.js` → view `src/marketing/banner/index.jsx` → dialog `src/marketing/components/banner/EditBannerModal.jsx`. Upload goes to Firebase Storage via `sendBannerToFirebase()` (`src/utils.js`, folder `popup_banner_img_path` = `images/popupBanner/`); a pasted URL also works when Storage rules block the upload.
- `BannerPopup` resolves in this order: panel record → `metadata/img.png` via `getBannerImageUrl()` → static `data/popupBanner.js` → nothing (the popup is not rendered at all).
- react-bootstrap 1.6 `Form.Check type="switch"` needs an explicit **`id`** (the input is visually hidden, so its `<label for=…>` only toggles it when the id matches) — see the banner and SEO modals.

## Marketing panel — blog management (Phase 4)
- Storage: `marketingPanel.blogDetails.posts[]` on the **`blog`** document (the same doc holds the `/blog-listing` SEO entry). Sub-schema `blogPostSchema` in `src/models/marketingPanelSchema.js`: `title, slug, excerpt, content, coverImage, author ("Marketing Team"), isPublished (true), publishedAt, updatedAt` (+ `_id` per post). No separate collection.
- Rules: slug is auto-generated from the title (`slugify`), unique across posts (validated on POST and PUT), and content is rendered as **plain text** on the website (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`).
- API: `pages/api/marketing/blog/index.js` (guarded GET/POST/PUT/DELETE — PUT also accepts just `{ _id, isPublished }` for the publish toggle) · `pages/api/marketing/blog/public.js` (public: list of published posts, or `?slug=` for one).
- Panel UI: dashboard tile `src/marketing/components/BlogManagementCard.jsx` → `pages/marketing/blog.js` → view `src/marketing/blog/index.jsx` → dialog `src/marketing/components/blog/EditBlogModal.jsx` (slug preview, counters, cover upload to `metadata/blogImg/` via `uploadBlogCover`).
- Website: `src/components/Demo-5/Demo5Blog1.js` renders the published posts (newest first, max 3) and **falls back to its original static cards** while loading or when the panel has no posts; each card links to `/blog/<slug>`.
- **`/our-blog` is the "Our Blog" listing page** (`pages/our-blog/index.js`): every published post with cover, date/author, excerpt and a "Read more" link; it is the breadcrumb target for the detail pages (`pages/our-blog/[slug].js`, breadcrumb `url="our-blog"`). `next.config.js` 308-redirects the old `/blog` and `/blog/:slug` to these routes.
- Cover images: uploaded from the panel to Firebase Storage **`metadata/blogImg/<slug>-<timestamp>.<ext>`** (`uploadBlogCover`) and stored in `marketingPanel.blogDetails.posts[].coverImage`. `normalizeCoverImage()` (`src/api/marketing/utils/blogPayload.js`) is applied on write and read: absolute URLs pass through, local paths get a leading slash (relative `images/x.jpg` breaks on nested routes), `imageUrl`/`featuredImage` payload aliases are accepted. Listing/detail components show `/images/blog/post-1-img.jpg` when a post has no cover or the URL fails (`onError`).
- `MARKETING_PAGES.blog` → `/our-blog`, so the listing page carries panel-managed SEO (`pages/our-blog/index.js` exports `getSeoStaticProps("/our-blog")` like the other managed pages).
- Helpers: `src/api/marketing/helpers/blogQueries.js`, payload rules in `src/api/marketing/utils/blogPayload.js` (`BLOG_LIMITS`, `slugify`, `sanitizeBlogPayload`); `api.marketingBlog` / `api.marketingBlogPublic` in `src/constant.js`.
- Deleting a post (`DELETE /api/marketing/blog?id=`) also removes its cover from Firebase Storage: the route parses the stored URL with `blogCoverPathFromUrl()` + `BLOG_COVER_FOLDER` (`src/api/marketing/helpers/blogCoverStorage.js`), deletes the file and returns `coverDeleted`. Foreign URLs (`/images/...`, external hosts, data: URIs) are skipped, and a missing file or Storage error only logs a warning — removing the record is never blocked. Only objects inside the blog cover folder can ever be deleted.
- ⚠️ **Import the Firebase SDK directly inside an API route** (`firebase/storage` + `lib/firebase`, as `pages/api/addDoctor.js` and `pages/api/doctor/upload-avatar.js` do). Importing it *through* a helper module (`src/services/firebaseStorage.js`, `lib/firebaseAdmin`, …) makes the route fail at runtime in dev with `TypeError: __webpack_require__.a is not a function` — pure helpers with no Firebase import are fine.

## Service descriptions (short copy for every service)
- Source of truth for the short copy: `data/serviceDescriptions.json` (service name → one line), read through `getServiceDescription(name)` in `src/customUtils/serviceLinks.js` (canonical key: lower-cased, `&`→`and`, gynecology/orthopedics spellings collapsed, so the static `gynecology & obs` finds the `Gynaecology & Obstetrics` entry).
- The same 20 strings were written to the `description` field of the 20 `servicesoffereds` rows in `IATRIC_test` (only that field — names/_id/categoryType and all other fields untouched). `mergeServiceLists` prefers the DB value, so a `description` edited in the super-admin panel wins over the JSON fallback.
- Rendered in the marquee service cards (`Demo5Services1` = MAJOR, `Demo5Services2` = speciality; both use `.service-card-desc`, clamped to 3 lines because `.service-card` is a fixed 240×260) and as the lead paragraph of `/service-details` (`ServiceDetailsComponent`, fallback **and** content branches).
- Re-seed after editing the JSON: `node -e '...'` pattern used in this session — connect to `MONGO_URI`, `updateOne({_id}, {$set:{description}})` per row, matching rows to the JSON by exact service name.

## Service links & mobile menu
- Canonical helpers live in `src/customUtils/serviceLinks.js`: `serviceDetailsPath({ name, service })` → `/service-details?name=<clean encoded name>&Service=<content key>` and `departmentPath(name)` → `/department-single?serviceName=<clean encoded name>`. Never pass a raw index/id (the old `&id=<index>` in `handleServiceClick` is gone).
- `/service-details` shows the clean service name in the breadcrumb (`resolveServiceName`) and heading, and picks its content block with `resolveServiceKey`; a service without a content block now renders a generic name + booking CTA instead of "Service Not Found".
- Writers: `Header1` service dropdown, `Demo5Services1` cards, `discover-more/DiscoverMore`, `Demo5Services2` (via `handleServiceClick` in `Common/commonMethod.js`).
- `MobileMenu`: "Services" is an **in-place accordion** (no navigation) listing the services from `useGlobalData()`; tapping one navigates with the clean URL and closes the drawer, "← Back to main menu" collapses it. Note the homepage banner popup is a modal with a higher z-index, so it must be dismissed before the drawer can be tapped.

## Reviews / testimonials (standardised)

## Homepage banner popup
- ONE image; source order: the marketing panel banner (`marketingPanel.home.bannerPopup`) → `data/popupBanner.js` (static fallback) → nothing (the popup is not rendered at all). `POPUP_FALLBACK_IMAGE` (`/images/popup-placeholder.png`) is used when the chosen `url` fails to load (next/image `onError`).
- Mounted only in `pages/index.js` (route `/`, not `/demo-5`); shown once per browser session via `sessionStorage: popup_banner_shown`.
- Closes ONLY via its × button (`backdrop="static"`, `keyboard={false}`) — backdrop clicks, ESC and banner clicks must not dismiss it.
- **Performance (image is on screen the moment the modal opens):**
  - The banner URL is resolved **server-side** by `getBannerForStaticProps()` (`src/api/marketing/helpers/bannerServer.js`) and passed as `initialBanner` from the homepage's `getStaticProps`, so `/` builds as `● ISR 60s` and the URL is already in the HTML (`BannerPopup` then skips its API fetch). The banner PUT calls `res.revalidate("/")`, so a panel save is live immediately instead of after the ISR window.
  - As soon as `BannerPopup` knows the popup will be shown (and the session flag is unset), it renders an **off-screen `priority` `<Image>`** with the same `src`/`sizes` as the modal (`POPUP_SIZES`). The browser therefore starts the exact `/_next/image` request ~0.8s before the modal opens and Next also emits the `<link rel="preload" as="image">` hint; the modal then paints from cache. Both copies must keep the same `sizes`, otherwise the URLs differ and there is no cache hit.
  - `next.config.js` → `images.minimumCacheTTL` is one year. Combined with the `?v=<lastUpdated>` buster this makes repeat visits pure cache hits (measured: `transferSize: 0`); cache entries optimised *before* that config change keep their old 60s TTL until they expire.
  - Uploads are shrunk/re-encoded to WebP client-side (see the Firebase bullet above) — a 3 MB PNG no longer ships to the browser.
- Additional image hosts must be added to `images.remotePatterns` in `next.config.js` (`firebasestorage.googleapis.com` is already allowed).

## Doctor profile photos
- Doctor Panel photo edits: `RegisterDocLoginHeader.handleSaveDoctor` POSTs the picked `File` to **`/api/doctor/upload-avatar`** (multipart, field `profilePicture` + optional `doctorId`) and puts the returned **URL** into the approval request. The route stores the photo at `images/doctorPicture/<doctorId|doctor>-<timestamp>.<ext>` (700×700 via the shared `resizeImage`, long-lived `cacheControl`, same folder as the super-admin flow) and does **no** DB writes or deletions — the live photo changes only when a super-admin approves the request.
- Why this exists: `changedFields` is sent as JSON and a `File` serialises to `{}`, so a Doctor Panel photo change used to be silently dropped. The panel now shows an "Uploading your profile photo…" status; if the upload fails it still submits the other profile changes. Optional guards on the route: `AVATAR_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (default 8 MB → 413), mime whitelist (415), `AVATAR_API_TOKEN` vs the `x-avatar-token` header, `AVATAR_STORAGE_FOLDER` override.
- Super-admin / onboarding uploads are unchanged: `pages/api/addDoctor.js` (POST create + PUT edit) resizes and uploads to the same folder itself.
- There is **no AI processing** on uploads: the AI white-coat experiment was reverted. (If it is ever revisited: DeepSeek has no image endpoint — it is text-only — and the `OPENAI_API_KEY` currently in `.env` is invalid; an image-capable key is required.)

## Doctor data migration script (`scripts/cleanDoctorEducation.js`)
- One-off CommonJS script (not part of the Next build, not linted by `next lint`) that upgrades every `doctors` document to the new `educationTraining` shape. `npm run db:clean-education` (dry run, the default — nothing is written) and `npm run db:clean-education:apply`; flags: `--apply`, `--reset` (store `[]` for every doctor instead of converting), `--limit=N`, `--backup=PATH` (JSON of `{_id, name, before, after}` written before the writes), `--uri=`, `--quiet`, `--help`.
- Reads `MONGO_URI` from the real environment first and falls back to `./.env` (hand-rolled reader, same intent as the removed `runSheetTasks.js`); `mongoose` is resolved from the repo so the script runs from any cwd. It prints db/host/collection (`IATRIC_test` ▸ `doctors`), the before/after of every change and a final verification pass (every value must be an array of trimmed, non-empty strings) that fails the exit code only on an `--apply` run.
- Writes go through the **raw driver** (`connection.collection("doctors").bulkWrite`) with a single `$set`, on purpose: pre-existing documents may be missing other (now required) fields, so a schema-validated `findByIdAndUpdate` would reject them. The splitting rules mirror `parseEducationTraining` (newlines/semicolons, bullet prefixes, never commas) because `src/customUtils/educationTraining.js` is ESM and cannot be `require`d from CommonJS.
- Pending `docdetailschangerequests` rows keep a snapshot in `updatedFields` and are applied verbatim on approval, so the script only *warns* about a string snapshot there instead of rewriting it.

## Sheet tasks → DeepSeek runner (`scripts/runSheetTasks.js`)
- Standalone CommonJS Node script (not part of the Next build): reads a task list from a Google Sheet and hands every task to the DeepSeek chat API **one at a time, in row order**, appending one JSON object per task. `npm run tasks:process`, `npm run tasks:process:dry`, or `node scripts/runSheetTasks.js --sheet=Tasks --limit=5 --dry-run`; `--list-sheets` prints the tabs, `--csv=PATH` reads a local CSV, `--mock` fakes responses.
- Input auth mirrors `logErrorToGoogleSheet` in `pages/api/helper.js`: `google-auth-library` JWT built from `serviceAccountKey.json` + `google-spreadsheet`. **`google-spreadsheet` v5 is ESM-only, so the script loads it with a dynamic `import()`** — `require()` throws `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`. Dependencies used are all pre-existing (`axios`, `google-auth-library`, `google-spreadsheet`).
- Env (read from `./.env`, real env vars always win): `TASKS_SHEET_ID` (falls back to `GOOGLE_SHEET_ID`), `TASKS_SHEET_NAME` (default `Tasks`), `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` (required unless `--mock`), optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` (default `https://api.deepseek.com`), `DEEPSEEK_MODEL` (`deepseek-chat`), `DEEPSEEK_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `DEEPSEEK_TEMPERATURE`, `DEEPSEEK_MAX_TOKENS`, `DEEPSEEK_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DEEPSEEK_RETRIES`, `TASKS_DELAY_MS`. The spreadsheet must be shared with the `client_email` inside `serviceAccountKey.json`.
- Sheet contract: header row with a task column (`Task | Prompt | Task Description | Description | Query | Question`, else column A) and optional `Context`, `Status`, `Result`, `Task Id`; `{{Header}}` placeholders in the task text are resolved from the row; rows with Status done/completed/success are skipped unless `--force`.
- Behaviour: strictly sequential (no concurrency), retries 429/5xx with exponential backoff + `Retry-After`, fails fast on other 4xx, `--resume` skips tasks recorded in `logs/sheet-tasks-state.json`, `--write-back` fills Status/Result when those headers exist, SIGINT finishes the in-flight task before stopping. Output: `logs/sheet-tasks-<timestamp>.jsonl` (gitignored).
- Safety: the default tab is **not** `GOOGLE_SHEET_NAME` on purpose — that points at the app's `ErrorLogs` tab, which must never be processed as tasks.

## E2E — meeting-room suite (Playwright)
- `tests/e2e/meeting-url.spec.ts` + `tests/e2e/helpers/meeting-room.ts` cover `/meeting/patient|doctor/:meetingId` (audio-only vs video, controls, roles, lifecycle). Hermetic: `**/api/getAppointmentId/**` is fulfilled from a fixture and `page.routeWebSocket` mocks engine.io v4 + socket.io v4 — `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL` points at production, so a test must never let a real socket connect.
- `installMeetingMedia()` records every `getUserMedia(constraints)` in `window.__mediaRequests`, which is how "an audio-only consultation never asks for video" is proven. Chromium always uses Playwright's fake devices; Firefox gets a synthetic `canvas.captureStream()` + WebAudio stream, because Playwright's Firefox never settles a native `getUserMedia` (no `firefoxUserPrefs` combination fixes it, headed or headless); WebKit gets fake devices on macOS but the same synthetic stream on Linux (see the CI trap below) — `needsSyntheticMedia(browserName)` picks the path, and `E2E_SYNTHETIC_MEDIA=1` forces synthetic locally so the Linux code path can be validated on macOS.
- CI trap (fixed): `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream` is a **Chromium** flag. Playwright's macOS WebKit tolerates it, but the Linux shell (`webkit-2359/pw_run.sh`) aborts the launch — `Cannot parse arguments: Unknown option --use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, exit code 1 → `browserType.launch: Target page, context or browser has been closed` — so **every test of the 4 WebKit projects (36 tests) failed instantly on GitHub Actions**, retries included, while the same suite was green locally. `WEBKIT_FAKE_MEDIA` in `playwright.config.ts` is therefore `process.platform === 'darwin' ? { args: [...] } : {}`. The `<gracefully close start> … <gracefully close end>` lines in the CI log are just the shutdown of an already-dead browser, never the cause.
- WebKit trap: Playwright's WebKit installs its mock `getUserMedia` from a document-start script that runs **after** `addInitScript`, silently replacing any patch (`String(navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia)` reverts to `[native code]` while the page still gets a fake stream). `install()` therefore caches the original binding once, is re-applied from a bounded 100 ms guard, and `window.__mediaInstrumented` exists to verify the patch is live.
- At ≤768px the side panel is a full-screen overlay that covers the control bar: close the panel before clicking control-bar buttons (`openMeeting` already closes it once).
- Full run: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/meeting-url.spec.ts` → 72 tests (8 × 9 projects: Desktop Chrome / Chrome FullHD / Firefox / WebKit, Mobile Chrome / Safari, Tablet Chrome / Safari / Safari Landscape), ~1.6 min.

## E2E — appointment suite (Playwright)
- `tests/appointment.spec.ts` walks `/appointment` end to end (form → mocked WhatsApp OTP → stubbed sandbox Cashfree checkout → `/payment/thankyou` → confirmation modal, plus the `?appointmentId=` return path); 9 tests (1 × 9 projects).
- First-paint trap (fixed): the whole app body renders **client-side** — `pages/_app.js` wraps it in `<NoSsr>` + redux-persist `<PersistGate loading={null}>` — so a cold document paints nothing at all (no header, no footer, not even the dark `Preloader` overlay) until the dev bundle has run. A full matrix run (81 tests, 9 projects, one dev server) pushed that past the config `expect.timeout = 15_000` and Mobile Safari failed `getByRole('heading', { name: 'Make Appointment' })` on a blank white page. The spec now asserts the first element of every freshly loaded document with `PAGE_READY_TIMEOUT = 60_000` (same idea as `openMeeting()` in `tests/e2e/helpers/meeting-room.ts`, which uses `timeout: 30_000` after `page.goto`). This is a test-budget fix, not an app bug — the page boots in seconds when the dev server is not saturated.
- Full matrix: `npx playwright test tests/appointment.spec.ts tests/e2e/meeting-url.spec.ts` → 81 tests (9 × 9 projects), ~3.1 min, all green.
- `npx next lint` / `tsc` do not cover `tests/` (`tsconfig.json` excludes it), so a spec change is validated by running the suite.
